clue.text: Resign as a result of dislocated vertebrae

parts.note: the vertebrae together make up the back, or spine
a dislocated joint is said to be out

explanation.surface: Someone forced to quit their job because of a slipped disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To back out is to withdraw from a commitment, much as one who resigns steps away from a post.

clue.text: Food served up by a woman resident in the town

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word for food is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: grub is slang for food
her stands for any woman

explanation.surface: A townswoman being handed a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgher is a citizen of a borough or town, especially a prosperous one.

clue.text: Presenting castle to the Duke of York is sweet

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for castle
Prince Andrew, long the Duke of York, is known informally as Andy

explanation.surface: Handing over a castle to a royal duke would be a lovely gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presenting ... to' joins the castle letter before the duke's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for sweets or confectionery.

clue.text: Sanction given by a self-righteous beast

parts.note: to OK something is to sanction or approve it
pi is informal for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Approval granted by a sanctimonious creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African forest animal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Can wrap present in it

indicators.note: the word for can wraps itself around the word for present, putting one inside the other

parts.note: a tin is a can
here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Instructions to put a gift in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the noun tin; 'present' looks like a gift but means here.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is an old-fashioned adverb meaning in that place or thing.

clue.text: Caught another train before father returned

indicators.note: another train suggests the letters of train made into a different arrangement
returned means the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A traveller boarded a different train before their father came home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges TRAIN into INATR; 'before' puts it ahead of AP, which is PA turned round by 'returned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone caught is trapped, so the idiom means captured or cornered.

clue.text: Offer to tighten watch-spring proves a disaster

parts.note: I'll, as in I'll do it, is an offer
to wind a watch is to tighten its spring

explanation.surface: Volunteering to wind someone's watch turns out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'Offer to tighten watch-spring' is someone saying I'll wind; 'proves' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill wind, from the proverb about it blowing nobody any good, is a misfortune or calamity.

clue.text: Jack ordered retsina; he certainly wouldn't!

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is a sailor too

indicators.note: ordered here signals the letters of the wine's name being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor asks for a glass of Greek wine, which a teetotaller would never do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns RETSINA into STAINER. 'Ordered' looks like asking for a drink at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller abstains from alcohol, so he would certainly never order wine.

clue.text: Demoted ambassador in debt to the bank

indicators.note: the envoy's word sits in the word for debt, inside it

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red, so red stands for debt
a legate is an envoy or ambassador, especially of the Pope

explanation.surface: An overdrawn diplomat is moved down the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To be relegated is to be moved to a lower rank or division.

clue.text: Penny made a syrup pudding featured in the paper

indicators.note: a pudding is a mixed-up mass, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny cooked a syrup sponge that got written up in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' scrambles A SYRUP into APYRUS. Penny looks like a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus was the reed-based writing material of ancient Egypt, an early form of paper.

clue.text: Be a campanologist! Does that sound familiar?

definitions.meaning: something that rings a bell seems familiar

explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer literally sounds a bell, and the idiom means to stir a memory.

clue.text: Sarah gets work in the Shrewsbury area

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sarah
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A woman gets a job in Shropshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Salop is an old name for Shropshire, an English county whose county town is Shrewsbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop is the traditional abbreviated name of Shropshire, the county around Shrewsbury.

clue.text: Putting fodder alongside electric cable is crazy

indicators.note: alongside puts the second piece next to the first

parts.note: hay is animal fodder
a wire is an electric cable

explanation.surface: Storing hay beside live wiring is madness.
explanation.definitionFit: To go haywire is to go out of control, behaving erratically or madly.

clue.text: How and why Grannie exploded?

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so the letters of Grannie are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A question about how an old woman lost her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' scrambles GRANNIE; the phrase also explains how and why she blew up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious acts with rage, which is both how and why Grannie blew up.

clue.text: Forbore to declare that the umpire was wet

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is an umpire
it rained when the weather was wet

explanation.surface: A complaint that the umpire was feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' looks like British slang for feeble, but it is rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to hold back from doing something, as one who refrains does.

clue.text: In all justice, the exhibition isn't too bad

parts.note: a fair is a show or exhibition
is not too bad is ''s fair', fair meaning reasonable

explanation.surface: A verdict that the show is passable.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'the fair's fair'; the 'S stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an appeal to fairness, used to insist on even-handed treatment.

clue.text: Make worse by keeping tank in delapidated garage

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the tank goes within the jumbled garage
a dilapidated building is falling apart, so the letters of garage are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquid

explanation.surface: A ruined garage is made worse by a tank kept inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delapidated' (so spelt in the clue) rearranges GARAGE into AGGRAE, and 'keeping' holds VAT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggravate a problem is to intensify it.

clue.text: Remarks on the absence of an educational journal

parts.note: no means none, an absence
TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British weekly for teachers

explanation.surface: Comments about a missing education paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are brief written comments or observations.

clue.text: Taking off a silver-plated brooch

indicators.note: plated means covered, so the word for silver goes around the word for brooch

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pin is a brooch

explanation.surface: A jewellery description: a pin coated in silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off someone means mimicking them, copying like an ape.

clue.text: Essentially consisting of articles and paintings

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: A gallery exhibition said to be basically writing and pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally, in one's true nature.

clue.text: Game that requires some backbone

parts.note: part means some of something
a ridge is a long raised backbone, as of a hill or roof

explanation.surface: A game requiring courage from players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backbone' looks like courage; 'Game' is the game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird shot for sport and food.

clue.text: Ostensible reason for the bardic tradition?

definitions.meaning: an excuse given to hide the true motive
bards passed on poems orally, before anything was written down

explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false justification, and split as pre-text it describes oral poetry predating writing.

clue.text: Supposed to have been laid in thatching material

indicators.note: laid in means placed within the thatching word

parts.note: reed is used for thatching roofs
put means laid or placed

explanation.surface: Something supposedly placed in the thatch of a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or said to be.

clue.text: English reader for an old German prince

parts.note: a lector is a reader, in church or a university

explanation.surface: An English academic reader serving a German royal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Elector was a prince of the Holy Roman Empire entitled to choose the emperor.

clue.text: Prisoner is taken to the house by coach

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, is a coach

explanation.surface: A captive is driven to a house by coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security.

clue.text: Young Peter suffers pain with flamboyance

parts.note: Peter Pan is the boy who never grows up
to ache is to suffer pain

explanation.surface: A boy called Peter is hurting but stays stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is dash and stylish confidence.

clue.text: Cites some of the Vietnamese

indicators.note: some of signals a run of letters taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A remark that some Vietnamese people are quoted.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite people is to mention them by name.

clue.text: Study notes in a dance

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
G is a musical note
A is another musical note

explanation.surface: Learning the music for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a long line.

clue.text: A question put to a university man in Jordan

definitions.note: the definition is a place in Jordan, standing for a noun

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone quizzes a graduate in Jordan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to' joins the question to the graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport, on the Red Sea.

clue.text: Various men sit, eat and drink in it

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of men, sit and eat in a different mixture

explanation.surface: Several men sit down to eat and drink in a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' scrambles MEN, SIT and EAT; the whole clue also pictures a cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French cafe or bar, a place to take a drink.

clue.text: Privates engulfed by a Midlands river in flood

indicators.note: engulfed by means the soldiers' letters are swallowed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a river through the English Midlands
OR, other ranks, means private soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers swept away by a river in spate.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rush of water, as in a flood.

clue.text: Pale and cold tranquillity." (Shelley)
